author: @Bekhouche

evidence.api_compatibility: No breaking changes. The four cost keys were silently dropped before, so nothing depended on them. GET /v1/models only gains optional fields. The new outputs.estimated_cost on routing decisions is additive — existing clients that do not read it are unaffected. The schema for /v1/models now includes the four cost fields, but as optional additions they do not break consumers that ignore unknown keys.
evidence.documentation: Comprehensive. New Cost metadata section in docs/guide/configuration/custom-models.md with four table rows and explanation of reporting vs routing, units (USD per million tokens), latency_ms_hint as author's estimate, re-registration erasure, and unusable-value warning. docs/api/router.md now describes outputs.estimated_cost with an example. docs/api/openai.md and docs/api/lemonade.md were regenerated for the new /v1/models fields. docs/guide/configuration/custom-models.md table entries for the four fields were added. The schema README was updated. The author also self-corrected CodeRabbit's two findings (model naming prefix on example key, and cost-selection claims that referenced non-existent features) in follow-up commits.
evidence.manual_release_testing: Four user-visible surfaces were added and no human appears to have exercised them end-to-end: (1) cost metadata persisted through POST /models/register, (2) cost metadata persisted through POST /pull, (3) cost fields listed on GET /v1/models, and (4) outputs.estimated_cost carried on routing decisions. The router cost-cache invalidation on registry generation change is tested in isolation but not through the HTTP path a user would follow. Maintainer to-dos cover these surfaces.
evidence.post_approval_commits: The PR merged via GitHub's merge queue; there are no post-approval commits on this PR's own branch. The post-approval-commits script returned commits from other PRs in the same merge group, which is expected behavior. The final approval on 2026-11-16 is the relevant one, and the merge commit (2026-11-21) reflects only reviewed changes.
evidence.review: PR #3518 was reviewed by @SlawomirNowaczyk, who has subject-matter expertise in the smart router (per docs/dev/contribute.md). He first requested changes on 2026-11-09 (major: docs referenced non-existent `cost_select`/`cost` classifier and `lemonade import` stripped cost keys; minor: missing cache test, config dir override, shared helper). The author addressed the major issues (docs rewritten on 2026-11-20, import fix, config_dir fix, shared header, router.md updated) and the reviewer approved on 2026-11-16. The final review confirmed: docs link to router.md which now describes estimated_cost, cache refresh is now tested, import covers collection models[] entries, Python tests use `next(..., None)` with a clear message, and temp dir cleanup is guarded. The review was thorough and applied project philosophy well.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The cost fields are user-defined, validated (cost_tier must be one of four bands; prices/latency must be non-negative numbers), and only reported or carried as metadata — they do not affect control flow, permissions, or network behavior. The new generation-counter cache invalidation is an internal mechanism with no external attack surface. No supply-chain, credential, or telemetry changes.
evidence.tests: A new 222-line C++ test (test_model_manager_cost_props.cpp) covers: registration preserves the four keys, router resolves registered cost, cost cache refresh after re-registration, typed price wins over extras, unusable values are dropped on read, unusable metadata names bad keys, and `lemonade import` keeps cost keys for both top-level models and collection components. Server-endpoint tests add test_000b (register through /models/register with cost fields, check /models lists them) and test_007a (pull through /pull with cost fields, check /models lists them). test_000a and test_000b were also improved to use `next(..., None)` with a clear assertion message instead of StopIteration. CI (C++ Server Build, Test, and Release) passed with conclusion success. No evidence of test weakening or inappropriate skipping.

maintainer_todos.text: Register a user model through POST /models/register with cost_tier, cost_input_per_million, cost_output_per_million and latency_ms_hint, then GET /v1/models and confirm all four fields appear in the model's entry.
Pull a user model through POST /pull with the same four cost fields, then GET /v1/models and confirm they are listed on the pulled model.
Send a POST /pull to re-register the same model with different cost values, then GET /v1/models and confirm the new values appear without restarting lemond.
Execute a routed request through the router and check that the response's outputs.estimated_cost carries the cost metadata (cost_tier, prices, latency_ms_hint) that was set on the selected model.

subject: fix(models): persist cost metadata through user-model registration (#3518)
summary: Adds cost_tier, cost_input_per_million, cost_output_per_million and latency_ms_hint to the USER_DEFINED_MODEL_PROPS and kKnownKeys allowlists, introduces a shared cost_metadata.h so the four keys survive POST /models/register, POST /pull, and `lemonade import`, lists them on GET /v1/models and in outputs.estimated_cost on routing decisions, and refreshes the router cost cache when the registry generation moves.
verdict_reason: The commit adds user-visible cost metadata to /v1/models, the /pull registration path, and routing decision outputs with a new cache-refresh mechanism, but nothing shows a human exercised these paths end-to-end before release.
